status_summary: The 2024 climate disclosure rules were stayed by the SEC on 2024-04-04 and have not taken effect. On 2025-03-27 the Commission voted to stop defending them, and on 2025-09-12 the Eighth Circuit held the consolidated challenges in abeyance until the SEC either reconsiders the rules through rulemaking or renews its defense. On 2026-05-29 the SEC proposed to rescind the rules entirely (Federal Register 2026-06-03, comments closed 2026-08-03); no final rescission had been published in the Federal Register as of 2026-10-18. No statute barring non-material ESG disclosure mandates was identified, though legislation was not searched in depth.

timeline.event: SEC votes to end its defense of the climate-related disclosure rules in the Eighth Circuit litigation.

The Eighth Circuit holds the consolidated petitions in abeyance until the SEC reconsiders the rules through notice-and-comment rulemaking or resumes defending them (order date and terms as stated in the SEC's 2026-06-03 proposal, which is a separate entry below).
SEC announces a proposal to rescind the climate-related disclosure rules in full.

Proposed rescission published in the Federal Register at 91 FR 33296 (File No. S7-2026-19, Release Nos. 33-11421 and 34-105572); comments due 2026-08-03. The SEC argues the rules exceed its disclosure authority and, alternatively, are unnecessary and costly.
SEC regulatory flexibility agenda (current as of 2026-05-12) lists the planned rescission.

title: Withdraw the SEC climate disclosure rule and bar non-material ESG disclosure mandates
uncertainties: The proposed rescission (91 FR 33296) was read in this review on federalregister.gov for its first 100,000 of 116,133 characters, which confirm the 2024-04-04 stay, the 2025-03-27 vote to end the defense, the 2025-09-12 abeyance order and the 2026-08-03 comment deadline; the SEC press release was read in full by the researcher. The Eighth Circuit order of 2025-09-12 is described through the SEC's own release and a docket summary, not the court docket. A Federal Register API query run in this review for SEC documents mentioning climate-related since 2026-06-04 returned only the 2026-08-14 Regulatory Flexibility Agenda, and one web search for a final adoption returned only law-firm summaries of the proposal, so no final rescission is found through 2026-10-18. An SEC press release listing fetched by the researcher was stale and was not used as evidence of absence, and the sec.gov page for File No. S7-2026-19 returned a fetch error. Any Commission vote not yet published, any Eighth Circuit action after 2025-09-12 and any pending bill to bar non-material ESG disclosure were not verified. The Mandate endnotes on human capital and board diversity were not checked.
